newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOOT ROOM ERA ABOUT TO END AT LIVERPOOL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOOT ROOM ERA ABOUT TO END AT LIVERPOOL.

text.p: Liverpool's famous Boot Room traditions -- founded by the late Bill Shankly almost 40 years ago -- are set to be swept away during a summer of change at Anfield.
The Boot Room was the tiny inner sanctum close to the dressing rooms where Shankly and his coaching staff would sit on benches amid the players' boots and kit and plot their tactics.
After Shankly retired in 1974, his deputy Bob Paisley took control of the club and went on to become the most successful manager in the history of English soccer.

Current manager Roy Evans also learnt much of his thinking in the Boot Room but Liverpool's 3-1 defeat at home to Manchester United on Saturday, which has realistically killed off their title hopes for this season, has heralded a change of thinking at the club.
The original Boot Room itself no longer exists but the club will finally break with its traditions during the close season.
For the first time since Shankly himself came to Liverpool in December 1959, the club are expected to appoint a new coach with no previous connections to the club in the summer.
The new man will work alongside Evans in the summer and Liverpool are believed to be seeking an experienced coach with a widespread knowledge of the European scene.
While a shake-up is planned in the Boot Room, at least four senior players also look set to leave after the club's failure to win the title for the first time since 1990.

Stan Collymore, Neil Ruddock, Phil Babb, possibly Jamie Redknapp and 20-year-old Mark Kennedy, who has never settled since a two-million-pound ($3.3-million) move from Millwall two years ago, could all be on the move.
Saturday's loss to United proved that while Liverpool have played some outstanding football this season, Manchester United are without doubt the best team in England.
Two goals from Gary Pallister, one from Andy Cole and some more error-riddled goalkeeping from David James ensured United's victory, their biggest at Anfield since 1969.
The win means that United need only five points from their final four matches -- which are to be played in a nine-day period next month -- to secure their fourth title in five years.
United could still achieve a double of league and European Cup triumphs this season if they overcome Borussia Dortmund in the second leg of their European Cup semifinal at Old Trafford on Wednesday.
For Liverpool, the title challenge is all but at an end but their season is not yet over.

They could still finish second to qualify for the Champions' League next season and could even turn around their 3-0 first-leg deficit and beat Paris St Germain on Wednesday to qualify for the European Cup Winners' Cup final though that seems unlikely.
